facts.title: Surprise behaviours go through one rarity gate, sp_roll
facts.fact: ma2_bot_surprise.c sp_roll_p is the only way a surprise trick starts. Order: trick switch (master RECOMP_BOT_SURPRISE / [Bots] Surprises, then RECOMP_BOT_SP_<NAME> / Sp<Name>); 20 s hold-off per bot per trick; per-bot cooldown (cool_min x 0.7-1.3); the random roll p[skill]; per-victim budget (2 per rolling 600 s, per trick); no same trick on the same victim back-to-back (not applied to side keys 0xFFFF0000|nation); 45 s spacing per victim. Counters go to [C7] sp_all (rolls, blocked_cool/budget/repeat/spacing, victim_human, trick_s, bot_s, tick_ms).
facts.how_to_use: RECOMP_BOT_SURPRISE=0 turns every surprise off (A/B arm). RECOMP_BOT_SP_FORCE=revenge,grudge,mood,rookie|all makes p=1 and skips cooldown/budget/repeat/spacing (trigger conditions still apply).

facts.title: Killer of a player = the scoreboard kill (stat 2) that went up within 1 s
facts.fact: sp_world_tick diffs each slot's kills/deaths once per frame, keeps a ring of kill events and death events, and matches each death with the nearest unused enemy kill within +-1 s (an enemy by nation in team modes). A death with no kill after 0.4 s is resolved with an unknown killer. Position of the victim is its last live position. Same attribution idea as hg_kills (high ground).
facts.how_to_use: RECOMP_BOT_SP_DIAG_KILLER=1 logs [SP-KILL] per death with victim and killer slots.

facts.title: Revenge on a teammate's killer (12)
facts.fact: A bot that sees a teammate die within 80 m (inside its field of view and a budgeted ray clear) rolls; the first witness to pass becomes the avenger for 30 s. The killer's target score is x1.3/1.5/1.8/2.0 by skill, the hunt pick weighs him x8 and always hunts, and an knowledge entry is injected at the death spot. Not for pilots on foot, objective locks or vehicle trips. C7 sp_revenge: witnessed, fired_<skill>, found (killer visible within 15 s), avenged, avenger_died. Forced run: 9 witnessed, 9 fired, 8 found.
facts.how_to_use: RECOMP_BOT_SP_REVENGE=0 / [Bots] SpRevenge=0

facts.title: Grudge: same killer twice within 5 min
facts.fact: On our death the killer is stored; a second death to the same player within 300 s rolls a grudge. After the next spawn, for 60 s that player's target score is x1.3-1.9 and his hunt weight x2; an entry is seeded at the killer's position. Ends on a kill of him (paid_back), our next death, or 60 s. C7 sp_grudge: armed, fired_<skill>, paid_back, expired, grudge_s_sum, grudge_kills, grudge_alive_s. Forced run (first death arms): 37 fired, 3 paid back (8 %), so the spec's 25 % payback line is not met by this mild bias.
facts.how_to_use: RECOMP_BOT_SP_GRUDGE=0 / [Bots] SpGrudge=0

facts.title: Momentum mood: HOT after 3 kills, COLD after 3 deaths
facts.fact: One roll per streak (the kill/death that makes streak 3; COLD waits for the respawn), p 0.5/0.45/0.35/0.25, budget key per side. 60 s. HOT: aggr +0.25, retreat_hp x0.8, flank chance x1.5 (flank_try), fight_band x0.85. COLD: caution +0.3, retreat_hp x1.2, G_COVER floor 0.92 when hurt (<75 %) and under fire. HOT ends on death, COLD on a kill. Deltas are applied to b->aggr/caution/sk.retreat_hp and subtracted at the end. C7 sp_mood: hot_/cold_<skill>, hot_/cold_/base_ kills, deaths, seconds, attack and cover seconds. RECOMP_BOT_SP_MOOD_STREAK=2 shortens the streak for tests.
facts.how_to_use: RECOMP_BOT_SP_MOOD=0 / [Bots] SpMood=0

facts.title: Rookie mistakes A-F (Recruit p 0.12, Regular 0.04)

A NaN/inf/huge header could spin that loop or size the allocation from UB, so the scan now bails (state 2, no roofs) unless 0 < cell < 1000 and the map is under 100 km, and the step is capped at 200 m. facts.title: A BattleArmor wall climb in progress no longer leaks into the next body
facts.fact: BotCtrl.co_phase (x2 wall climb) survived a body change. If the BA died or was boarded away while latched (phase 3), the next climb_order call ran ba_release on the NEW actor (a pilot or Mech), calling the claw-release routine on an object that is not a BattleArmor. The new-body block in ma2_bot_ctrl.c now clears co_phase, co_done, co_res, the stick axis and climb_state.

facts.title: Level never shoots a building of its own side
facts.fact: Ma2BldView gained nation (actor_int +0xA8, the same read objective_update uses; 1/2 = team, -1 unknown). spc_level_look returns when v.nation == me->nation, so an Elite whose enemy ducked behind a team building (Base War, own base) does not level it. The kill-delta loop in sp_world_tick is also capped to SP_KEV events per frame so a scoreboard jump cannot spin it.

facts.title: Roof scan: 400 surface rays per game step, RF_MAX 192 roofs, flood fill of cells 8 m over terrain
facts.fact: ma2_bots_core.c roofs_step/roofs_finish (push-x2): once per map, after the nav grid is ready, samples surface_height on a <=300k-cell grid (5 m step on UC), flood-fills cells >= 8 m above the terrain into blobs, and keeps blobs of >= 6 cells whose flat top is >= 10 m over ground as one stand point each. sn_roofs returns the nearest 8 within maxd and re-checks each with one surface ray (a destroyed building drops out). facts.title: VtolTwoRiders: a bot VTOL holds for and carries two BattleArmor (the player + a bot)
facts.fact: Default on. VtolMuster now holds while fewer than two ride (never with their flag carrier aboard), prefers the player over a nearer bot, also over a lift request from a BattleArmor within 50 m, and also on its own flag run at pickup/inbound when 400 m or more from their flag (MusterWhere's 200 m rule kept). order_lift with one rider aboard hovers for the second via lift_hold (bot: 9 m + 1.5 m so the hanging rider clears the ground; player: 12 m over him, 12 m ahead), or fetches the run's BattleArmor within 150 m with the player aboard (else that run ends, 'too far to fetch'). frun_consider still rolls while holding for the player, so a bot partner comes too.

facts.title: g_frun[n].ba2: the second BattleArmor on a flag run; whoever takes the flag is flown home
facts.fact: When the run's VTOL carries a rider that is not g_frun.ba, the VTOL eval records it as ba2 ([BOT-TWORIDERS] joins the flag run). frun_member counts ba2, so a bot ba2 gets order_ride's flagrun-drop over their flag, and frun_eval sends it to OP_GRAB in FR_GRAB. frun_step swaps ba/ba2 (.human) when ba2 carries their flag ('second_carries') or when ba is lost ('second_takes_over'), so FR_EXTRACT fetches the actual carrier. Proven: player + bot flown , the bot took the flag and was flown home and captured (test wa2r3 11-01); in wa2r4 the player took it, captured as a player run.

facts.title: Two BattleArmor can clamp onto one VTOL at once (rider list actor+0x1A8)
facts.fact: The VTOL rider vector (12-byte entries at actor+0x1A8.+0x1AC) takes a second BattleArmor: a bot clamped (ba_clamp, 10.9-11.0 m horizontal) under a VTOL already carrying the player; both stayed on for the 18 s flight to their flag and both were set down there. Hovering 10.5 m over the bot (cargo 3 + 1.5 m) the player hung 1-4 m off the ground and was not knocked off.

facts.title: A bot BattleArmor no longer boards a mustering VTOL for a ride shorter than 150 m
facts.fact: order_ride lets a generic rider go within 150 m of its lift destination, so a bot BattleArmor standing beside a VTOL at our stand after a capture was mustered, clawed on, let go at once and reclawed every 2 s (BaReclaw). Under VtolTwoRiders the BA side skips the muster when its lift destination (or objective / roam point) is within 150 m and it is not carrying their flag ([C7] tworiders muster_short_hop_skipped).

facts.title: BaHackClose: per-skill NeuroHack odds for an enemy 'Mech within 25 m, +15 points against the player
facts.fact: Default on (playtest 11-01). The hack pick was a bare utility race (1.0 under 45 m) that an Elite already in G_ATTACK never lost (~0.87 + 0.15 hysteresis). Now an engageable enemy 'Mech within 25 m (BA health >= 0.35, not hacked in the last 30 s) is rolled for once per encounter: Recruit 45%, Regular 60%, Veteran 75%, Elite 85%, +15 points (cap 95%) against the human's 'Mech. A win sets s[G_HACK] = 1.4 for that 'Mech while it stays within 25 m; F19's commit then holds the hack. The result is kept per memory slot; a new roll needs another 'Mech, or this one out of 25 m for 5 s and the last roll 5 s old. A loss leaves the old rules.

facts.title: Test hooks RECOMP_TEST_BOT_BA / RECOMP_TEST_BOT_VTOL / RECOMP_TEST_HFERRY_REACH
facts.fact: RECOMP_TEST_BOT_BA=<bot index> / RECOMP_TEST_BOT_VTOL=<bot index> set that bot's preference for a BattleArmor / VTOL to 3.0 in vehicle_pref_b (it takes and keeps one; a vehicle_value bonus alone was swapped away). facts.title: A 'Mech death blast goes off 2.2 s after its health reaches 0 and kills out to ~45-50 m
facts.fact: Measured over 269 MCP test matches ([DEATH] pairs + [BOT-BLAST]): units within 60 m of a 'Mech that goes down die 2.2-2.3 s after its health reaches 0 (609 of the nearby deaths in that bin; 52 of 63 at exactly +2.2 s from hp zero); 120-400 m apart the timing is flat, so it is the blast. A second peak at +4.4 s is a chain (a 'Mech killed by the first blast blows 2.2 s later). Deaths by distance before any fleeing: 0-29 m ~60%, 30-39 m 40%, 40-49 m 29%, 50-59 m 18% (already-damaged units die further out). Core now models 45 m for 2.6 s (was 35 m for 6 s).

facts.title: A running 'Mech told to go behind itself plays a ~1 s pivot at walk pace; backing out is faster
facts.fact: MechAI MoveTo (mode 6, run=1) to a point behind a 'Mech running at full speed: actor+0x268 bit 0 (run) drops to 0 and anim 6 plays for ~1 s while it turns at ~walk pace, then anim 1, then anim 2 (run) again (trace game-bA bot 2 t=24.4). A death-blast escape lost ~half its 2.2 s that way: escaping 'Mechs averaged 0.51 of top speed against 0.93 in normal travel. sub_2AD5C0 forward speed takes a SIGNED percent (cvtsi2ss * comp+0xBC * 0.01, clamped to +-comp+0xC0), so body_walk_direct(. -100) with the nose held on the hazard backs straight out with no pivot. A/B (RECOMP_TEST_FAKE_BLAST, ~48 escapes each): outward speed old 4.2, 80 m carrot 5.4, direct walk 3.1 (walk pace), back-out 6.6 m/s. CAUTION: driving a 'Mech backwards from the bot tick crashed a real match (game-bR1, t=144.7): wild guest write in the 'Mech animation update (MAMech vt slot 51 sub_FED88 -> +0x868 track table) while four 'Mechs backed out (anim 37). The campaign AI never reverses; do not ship a negative-speed drive without finding that fault.

facts.title: Death-blast escape fixes 11-01: BattleArmor hop out, 'Mechs back out, fire held, overrides closed
facts.fact: ctrl_bomb_escape: BattleArmor leave on jet hops (BlastHop; their MoveTo walk is 0 m/s, so a fleeing BA in a travel order stood still: 318 frames at speed 0 in one match); 'Mechs steer at a point 80 m out along the escape line (BlastDrive, RECOMP_BOT_BLAST_DRIVE 0-3, default 1; 3 = back out, test only: it crashed a real match); no shots while leaving a death blast (BlastHoldFire). Reaction by skill now Recruit 0.4 / Regular 0.3 / Veteran 0.2 / Elite 0.1 s (was 0.6/0.4). Overrides closed: a pilot's own-pack run-off (bomb_flee_until) skipped the escape and then re-steered it to 32 m; a BattleArmor on a wall-climb order (climb_order returns first) never ran it. Test hook RECOMP_TEST_FAKE_BLAST=<s> puts a harmless blast 18 m ahead of the next bot every <s> s; scratch tools blastmon.py / fleespeed.py audit escapes from [TRACE].

facts.title: Reading the terrain type map at run time: [0x50C8E0] MATerrainInfo -> layer [+0x84] -> picture [+0xC]
facts.fact: sub_F7AC7(this = active MATerrainInfo [0x50C8E0], layer, category, x, z) tests a terrain category at a point: sub_F7A96 picks the layer [TI+0x84+layer*4] (layer 0 = the type map), sub_F7AA6 the category record [TI+0x88+(layer*11+cat)*4] (mask +0x10, shift +0x14), sub_189E62 turns the position into a picture cell (cell = picture width sub_267410 [pic+0x58] / (terrain samples [0x4EAF64]+4 x cell size +0x814) x position; height [pic+0x5C] likewise; picture = [layer+0xC], valid when [pic+0x38] != 0) and sub_1899C6 -> sub_2674A0 reads the pixel at [pic+0x4C] + x*[pic+0x24] + z*[pic+0x50] (16-bit when [pic+0xC] & 7). The raw 16-bit value is the type (0 play, 1 out of bounds, 2 border, 8/16/32 water). ti_type_at in ma2_bot_ctrl.c reads it the same way natively.
facts.how_to_use: RECOMP_BOT_DIAG=1 RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_EDGE_DUMP=1 prints the map as the bot air planner sees it ([BOT-VEDGE] z= rows: # out of bounds, + border band, play).

facts.title: The out-of-bounds wall stands at the type-map 2/1 edge and holds at any height; band 2 also rims cliffs inside the arena
facts.fact: So the invisible wall is at the 2/1 edge, not the 0/2 edge, and VTOL height does not get past it. Deliverance's whole middle hill (85-100 m) is type 1: the playable area is the valley that bends round it. Type 2 is not only the outer rim: Bogged Down marks its plateau cliff faces inside the arena with 2, so 2 cells must stay passable for fliers.

facts.title: VtolLaneRoute: VTOL long legs planned on a 20 m air grid (valley/lane following, no gratuitous climbs)
facts.fact: In a playtest (11-01) Deliverance VTOLs climbed high over the hill instead of following the valleys. Legs of 150 m+ are planned by an A* on a 20 m grid built once a match from the walk grid's surface (highest per cell): cost = length x lane factor (0.9 on a lane, 0.75 on the flight's favoured lane) x (1 + height over max(start, goal height)/K) + 2 per metre climbed, then pulled tight where the straight cut stands no more than `slack` over the cells it replaces. A goal on a plateau costs nothing extra (Bogged Down ferry 848 m vs 834 m straight); a wide high crossing costs about a 1.5x valley detour. Routes needing a climb past a learned cap or 90 m still take the ground route; short legs stay VtolTerrainClimb's straight line. Before: Deliverance VTOLs at 104-107 m over the hill (max_y 107.6, ground_tall 25 a match); after: ferries along the valley at a median 28-36 m, flag runs completed inbound -> grab -> extract with the rider on. Plans cost 1-2.6 ms max.
facts.how_to_use: RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_LANE_ROUTE=0 / [Bots] VtolLaneRoute=0 restores the straight leg. RECOMP_BOT_DIAG: [BOT-VROUTE] per plan (straight vs route length, hi400, closest edge, roll, points). [C7] vtlane: plans, bends, straight, fail, lane_s, plan_ms, ground_tall/ceiling.

facts.title: VtolRouteVary: each VTOL flight rolls its own route (K, lane, cost field, corner slack, cruise band)
facts.fact: In a playtest (11-01) every VTOL flight between the same two points took the same route. A flight (a goal 80 m+ from the last, or 90 s on) rolls K 45-90 (rider caps it at 50), a favoured lane (30% none), a smooth +-35% cost field on a 160 m lattice, slack 6-18 m (10 with a rider) and a cruise band 0-12 m (4 with a rider), seeded from the clock per match, the bot and the flight count; replans keep the roll (no jitter). Over four Deliverance runs the north-base-to-west-flag flights left the base by different exits (east round 1590,350-1590,470 or straight SW by 1430,430 / 1290,590) and cut the valley corner differently.

facts.title: VtolEdgeKeep: VTOL routes keep off type-map out-of-bounds cells (general, any map incl. custom)
facts.fact: In a playtest (11-01) VTOLs flew right up to the invisible wall on the tall cliff tops, exploiting the map edge. The air grid marks cells with any type-1 sample (4 m sampling) as out of bounds and band-only cells as border; routes never cross out-of-bounds cells, keep 25 m off them (waived within 60 m of start/goal; over a band now, the way out is open), pay up to x2.5 within 60 m and x1.5 on band cells; a goal on an out-of-bounds cell is moved to the nearest cell 20 m+ inside (a retreat spot on Deliverance's hill had sent a VTOL to 111 m against the wall); fight hide/slide spots keep 25 m off. Measured per flight ([BOT-VEDGE] closest approach to type-1): Deliverance final run over_oob_s 0.5 s / 180 s (0.5 s while hovering cover near the west flag), Ill Wind 0, Bogged Down 0; closest approaches under 20 m only at flags that sit near the edge.

facts.title: BaHackFlee: bot 'Mechs leave an enemy BattleArmor inside 18 m like a death blast
facts.fact: A successful NeuroHack is an instant kill, so 'Mechs move away from a BattleArmor at close range as they do from a self-destructing 'Mech (playtest 11-01). In ctrl_bomb_escape every alive enemy BattleArmor within 18 m (and 15 m of height), not riding a VTOL and not clamped to anyone, is a hazard of radius 26 m with the death blast's reaction by skill; not once one is clamped on (the QTE code answers that). Verified: [BOT-BOMBAV] '(enemy BattleArmor)' escapes in every 5v6 CTF run (Deliverance 7 in one match, by skills 0/2/3), and one from the human's BattleArmor on Bogged Down (vs_human=1).

facts.title: VtolEdgeAll: every VTOL steer target and leg keeps off the type map's out-of-bounds cells (25 m, more when high)
facts.fact: In a playtest (11-01) bot VTOLs still hugged the map edge, on custom maps too. VtolEdgeKeep covered only long planned legs. VtolEdgeAll builds a distance field at the type map's own resolution (MATerrainInfo [0x50C8E0] layer +0x84 picture +0xC; bit 1 = out of bounds; Deliverance 512x512 at 4 m, built in 1.5-3.3 ms) and keeps every VTOL goal, carrot and cargo hover off it (25 m; 10 m for hook/drop tether work), the keep growing 1 m per metre over 20 m above the ground (to 55 m). A point in the band moves up the field's slope (the edge normal), else to the nearest ring point clear. Every route (air A*, straight short leg, ground route) has its corners kept in and gets a bend where a leg dips 3 m+ into the band (not the way out of a band it starts ). The missile dodge flips away from the edge, and a craft that drifts in anyway (carried past its point, a firing hover where it stopped) is flown back out to 30 m. Measured 5v6 CTF, player ferried, off -> on: Deliverance closest approach 0.0 -> 34.3 m, 4.0 -> 0 s within 25 m, peak 61 -> 43 m up; Bogged Down 0.0 -> 29.6 m, 8.5 -> 0 s, high-near-edge 6.7 -> 0 s; the Bogged Down ferry still flew the plateau edge straight (767 m closed in 774 flown). Plain 5v6 Deliverance matches vary: 9.4 s within 25 m of 237 s airborne before the drift recovery, 1.0 s of 190 s after it. Follow-up: the route keep is 28 m, the recovery acts under 24 m and only 12 m+ up (MoveTo at 6 m held a craft taking off from a pad 8 s), and a craft closing on the edge fast is braked on the reversed stick (a firing hover let go at 58 m/s coasted 20 m over the line).

RECOMP_BOT_VTOL_TRACE=1 prints [BOT-VEDGE2] pos/agl/edge twice a second.

facts.title: VtolEdgeKeep's 20 m edge grid chamfer read unvisited neighbours: distances stopped two cells from out of bounds
facts.fact: In ag_build (ma2_bot_ctrl.c) the two chamfer passes used s = pass ? 1: -1 with neighbours i - s, so the forward pass read the right/below neighbours (not yet visited) and the backward pass the left/above ones: each pass moved a distance one cell, so g_ag.ed was exact only within ~40 m of out of bounds and 1e9 beyond (the 60 m cost ramp was cut at 40 m). The same pattern copied into the fine field left 1e9 beyond 8 m. Fixed (s = pass ? -1: 1) for the fine field always and for the 20 m grid under VtolEdgeAll.
facts.how_to_use: A two-pass chamfer must read only neighbours already visited in that pass's order.

facts.title: BaHackHop: BattleArmor walk is 0 m/s, so a hack needs aimed hops; the jump's direction ai+0x244 can be steered mid-burn
facts.fact: Why bot BattleArmor rarely clamped: a BA's MoveTo walk is 0 m/s and F19 blocked every hop inside 40 m of the 'Mech (a travel hop flew 52-65 m past it), so inside 40 m a hacking BA stood still and only clamped a 'Mech that walked up; BaHackFlee 'Mechs walk off at 18 m. BaHackHop hops at the 'Mech inside 60 m: aimed at its position + velocity x flight time x a skill lead share (0.35/0.6/0.85/1.0), steered during the burn by rewriting the StartJump direction ai+0x244/+0x24C (sub_18AD06 reads it every tick; turn rate 1.2-4 rad/s by skill), the burn cut by setting the end time ai+0x250 to now once the coast would carry it on, the next hop after a skill reaction and the fuel the distance needs (0.4 s + 1 s per 38 m), the claw tried every 0.15 s within 11 m. Vs the player lead and turn are 0.6x. Measured over 3 off / 4 on 5v6 CTF matches: won hack rolls 9 -> 12, clamps on 'Mechs 1 -> 7, NeuroHacks done 1 -> 6; all 7 claw tries inside 11 m took. A 'Mech running 17-22 m/s outruns the hops.
facts.how_to_use: RECOMP_BOT_BA_HACK_HOP=0 / [Bots] BaHackHop=0 = the old F19 approach. [C7] bahackhop: hops, hops_vs_player, steer_s, cuts, fuel_wait_s, tries_air/ground, refused_air/ground, clamps, clamps_vs_player, miss_m_sum/miss_n. [BOT-HACKHOP] per hop (DIAG).

facts.title: StartJump sub_18ABB5 jump state: ai+0x240 jumping, +0x244 unit direction, +0x250 end time, +0x254 duration, +0x258 strength
facts.fact: sub_18ABB5(ebx=ai; dir*, dur, str) needs jet fuel actor+0x49C > 1, clamps dur to the fuel, normalises dir (sub_464C0) into ai+0x244.+0x24C, sets ai+0x240 = 1, +0x258 = strength, +0x254 = duration and +0x250 = game time + duration. The per-tick jet flight sub_18AD06 (only under MoveTo / AI mode 6) reads +0x244/+0x248/+0x24C and +0x258 every tick and clears +0x240 once the time passes +0x250. Measured on a BattleArmor: ~24-27 m/s along the ground while airborne (burn and coast), gravity ~44 m/s2, fuel burns ~1/s and refills ~0.9/s, a 1.5 s burn flew ~65 m, an 0.85 s burn ~11 m; a body held in AI mode 7 (body_stop) does not fly a started jump.
facts.how_to_use: Steer a jump mid-burn by rewriting the x/z of ai+0x244 (keep it unit length); end the burn early with ai+0x250 = now.

facts.title: BaDipHop: a BattleArmor with somewhere to go that stays within 4 m for 3.5 s hops out toward the lowest rim
facts.fact: Logs 11-01 (Bogged Down) showed two shapes: (a) in a hollow under 20 m high ground, held in place by a stop each step so a started jump never flew, 11 s at 969,5,1247; (b) a drop leg begun mid-hop: drop_y0 was taken in the air, landing 8 m lower read as 'came down', so neither the 5 s give-up nor DropLedge's jet ran: 49 s at 886,17,1185 'stepping off'. BaDipHop: after any order step, a BA whose TRAVEL / FIGHT_MOVE / HACK / ENGAGE goal is away and that stayed within 4 m for 3.5 s (not jumping, not holding a partial route's end) waits for fuel 1.2, scores 12 bearings by the highest surface 4-20 m out plus 6 m per (1 - cos) off the route's next point, jets at that rim + 3 m and steers there under MoveTo until it lands; a drop attempt seen in the air restarts on landing. BA-heavy Bogged Down match: 2 stuck spells, 2 hops, both freed (8 m+ away 5 s later).

facts.title: Deliverance player ferry 'stall at the pickup' = the test hook's 8 m claw gate, plus a 45 s second-rider chase
facts.fact: (1) For 120 s no friendly bot flew a VTOL (all took 'Mechs): use RECOMP_TEST_BOT_VTOL. (2) The VTOL then came down 10 m off and 8 m up the standing human (lift-pickup; MoveTo settles short) and hung there 45 s, but the hook only tried the claw under 8 m horizontal: the game's clamp test sub_10239A accepts a friendly VTOL much further out (clamped at 13.0 m / 12.3 m up = 17.9 m 3D in wd_f1, refused at 13.0 m / 15.3 m up in wcdel0). (3) With the player aboard, the VTOL held for the run's bot BattleArmor, which chased it jetting 40-50 m away for 45 s; the hold's 8-11 s clock restarted every time the BA hopped out of 50 m, the run ended 'pickup too long' and was rolled again at once with the same BA (twice). The hook now tries the claw within 13 m / 16 m up and lets go within 30 m of their flag (up to 30 m up, as a player would); TwoWaitCap fixes (3). Proof wd_f1: clawed on at the base (1460,281), flown 1400 m to within 47-58 m of their flag at (357,1208).

facts.title: TwoWaitCap: a VTOL with one rider waits at most 12 s for a second, and rolls no run while the player hangs on
facts.fact: TwoWaitCap (RECOMP_BOT_TWO_WAIT_CAP / [Bots] TwoWaitCap, default on): (a) a VtolMuster hold that lapses under 4 s (the BattleArmor hopped out of 50 m) and comes back keeps its 8-11 s clock; (b) with one rider aboard, holding (lift_hold) or fetching the run's BattleArmor for a second rider lasts 12 s at most (two_wait_over), then the pickup run ends ('the second BattleArmor did not make it aboard', [C7] frun ends_second_missed), the hold is given up 45 s, no second hold for 30 s, and the one aboard is flown (the player's VtolWaitPlayer run); (c) frun_consider rolls no new run while the player hangs on (it used to restart the same pickup run with him aboard). Cause: a VTOL flying with a rider overshoots a moving BattleArmor at 20-50 m/s, so the BA never got under it (wbdel1, 100 s lost). [C7] twowaitcap capped_player_aboard / capped_bot_aboard / resumed / no_run_rider.

facts.title: PlayerRunHurt: a badly damaged VTOL carrying the player decides once -- press on to their flag, or set him down
facts.fact: Cause of the restart loop: frun_step ended the player's flag run when the VTOL fell below the give-up health (Recruit 0.5 / Regular 0.42 / Veteran 0.35 / Elite 0.28), and order_lift's VtolWaitPlayer start, which had no health test, began it again the next tick while he still hung on (wa2r4: 81 starts / 79 '0 s' damage ends in 10 s, [C7] frun started_player 13 / ends_damaged 11). PlayerRunHurt (RECOMP_BOT_PLAYER_RUN_HURT / [Bots] PlayerRunHurt, default on): with the player aboard the VTOL calls it once (hurt_decide, g_hurt[nation]): within Recruit 200 / Regular 280 / Veteran 360 / Elite 450 m of their flag it presses on (the run's damage end is skipped while he rides); further out it sets him down -- at our stand if within 350 m, else 150 m back toward it -- coming down low there (note lift-hurt-setdown, ends_damaged_setdown). The call stands while he hangs on (the lift goal is kept down to 8 % health) and 45 s after he lets go. Verified: wd_h3 (Bogged Down, Recruit VTOL set to 20 % 4 s after pickup, 828 m out) set him down at our stand 8 s later, one player-run start in the match; wd_f1 (Deliverance, Veteran at 34 %, 57 m out) pressed on.

facts.title: CaptureReset: a flag carrier's ride-home request ends at the capture, so its VTOL can start the next run
facts.fact: In a playtest (log 2026-11-01 match 2, Deliverance) the human scored while aboard, and the VTOL that carried him kept flying him back to his team's flag stand. Cause: g_lift requests are never cleared, and order_lift used lift_find(rider) whatever its age; the carrier's ride-home request (LiftHuman / LiftCarrier, and the flag run's extract post) still pointed at the team's own stand, so the rider got 'lift-fly' to 1364,861 instead of 'lift-to-flag', hovered there t=76-106, and VtolWaitPlayer (which needs no request) never started a new run. Fix (RECOMP_BOT_CAPTURE_RESET / [Bots] CaptureReset, default on): g_lift[].car marks a carrier's ride home (lift_post_carrier, frun_eval in FR_EXTRACT); order_lift drops it once the rider no longer carries their flag ([BOT-CAPRESET]); a bot rider that scored aboard gets a fresh FR_INBOUND run within 10 s, and order_ride restarts the rider's 60/90 s clock when it stops carrying. Also (TwoWaitCap c) our own solo cover run gives way when the player claws on. Verified wd_cap1 (Bogged Down, NOPOST + REACH): captured aboard at t=59.4, request (12 s old) dropped, '[text omitted]' at 59.4/60.0, orders lift-to-flag toward their flag. [C7] capreset carrier_lift_cleared_player / _bot, new_run_player / new_run_bot, rider_clock_reset.

facts.title: BlastWary: bots keep 40 m off a nearly dead 'Mech and wait outside a pending death blast
facts.fact: BlastWary (RECOMP_BOT_BLAST_WARY / [Bots] BlastWary, default on; brain blast_wary after the goal's order): every 'Mech's health is sampled every 0.25 s (g_mhp, 2 s ring) to get its time to 0 at the damage it is taking. A bot in a 'Mech or tank with a 'Mech within 55 m (either side, the player's too) at or under Recruit 5 / Regular 8 / Veteran 12 / Elite 15 % while hit, or gone within 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 / 2.5 s, notices it after its reaction time with 35 / 60 / 80 / 95 % (rolled once per dying 'Mech): fighting that 'Mech, the ENGAGE band starts at 40 m (ctrl_fight steps out inside band_min); within 30 m of any other dying 'Mech it moves out to ~48 m (FIGHT_MOVE, still firing); an order that would take it within 40 m slides round at its distance. The episode survives 2 s gaps in the dying reading, is capped at 8 s (then that 'Mech is ignored 20 s), and covers combat goals plus objective duty except the races (carry, grab, return, chase-it, bomb). BattleArmor do not claw onto it. Any ground bot just outside a pending blast (hp 0, <= 2.6 s; 45 m + hull) whose order goes nearer holds where it stands until it goes off, unless a dying 'Mech is within 30 m. Measured (real 5v6 CTF, no fake blasts): mixed skill, 7 runs ON vs 5 OFF: blast deaths 0.09 vs 0.29 per blast (4/47 vs 10/35), units inside 45 m when a blast goes off 0.21 vs 0.37 per blast; all-Regular (skill 1): no change (0.57 vs 0.57, small n). Kills/scores not skewed.

facts.title: VtolArrive: a VTOL bound for an exact stop brakes on a curve (the stick reversed) and with a rider sinks to drop height
facts.fact: on Deliverance a VTOL with a rider crossed the enemy base ~35 m up at up to ~80 m/s, overshot their flag 80-150 m and circled. The stick flight (vtol_manual) holds full forward thrust while the nose is on the point; MoveTo's cargo hover only takes over inside 14 m. vt_arrive (stick branch of ctrl_travel, stop <= 5 m, goal not overhead) holds forward speed to 4 + sqrt(2 x 20 m/s2 x the route left), latched once begun (unlatched it let go and sped up 66 -> 94 m/s), the stick reversed when faster (a reversed stick took 94 -> 42 m/s in 0.5 s), the drift across the nose steered to the point; with a rider aboard inside 90 m it sinks with comp+0x90 = -30 (a player's Ctrl) to 12 m over the drop point's ground (10 m over what stands under it). Human ferry, off -> on: Deliverance the player let go 30 m from their flag 25.6 -> 8.8 m up with the VTOL 34 -> 13 m up, ~60 -> 15 m/s; Bogged Down 13.6 -> 8.1 m up, 40 -> 23 m/s; both ~0.9 s after first coming within 60 m.

facts.title: SUPERSEDED: a bot VTOL ferrying a bot BattleArmor crawled 4-9 m/s at full stick -- NOT the height ceiling; real cause = stale AI forward speed (see vtol-ferry-stale-ai-forward-speed)
facts.fact: CORRECTION 2026-11-10: the 2026-11-04 "height ceiling" resolution was wrong. Real cause: the AI MoveTo of the rider pick-up hover left a forward-speed target on the flight comp (comp+0x98 = -53.4 m/s), and the body integrator sub_002AD940 adds heading x that ground speed to the stick flight velocity, so 60 m/s forward on the stick became ~6 m/s. Fixed in v26-vtol b91f768 (vtol_stick_take, StickSpeed0). Original observation kept: e1c20284, Bogged Down weB0, bot 10 (team 1) flew a bot rider (bot 6, BattleArmor, ord idle, ctl=attack, firing at a target) toward 495,903: stick branch, thr 1.00, err 0-3 deg, no climb demand (c90 0), y held at 47.2 (that match's max_y so far), speed 3.6-9.6 m/s from t=14 to ~79 s. Other bot-rider ferries flew 40-106 m/s. Cause not found; suspects: the rider's attack state pulling on the clamp, or a height cap. [BOT-VCRAWL] missed it because the speed jittered over 9 m/s; it now uses a 1.5 s smoothed speed. RESOLVED 2026-11-04: 47.2 m was Bogged Down's stick-flight ceiling there (terrain height + MaxVTOLHeight 55 - ~6.6; the stick cannot climb further), so the ferry at full stick could only press on level, slowed by whatever stood ahead at that height (cause inferred from the same picture; the ceiling and its terrain dependence measured 11-04). Fixed by StickCeil (the planner knows the ceiling) and RiderRay (real collision rays at ceiling - 9 m shut the way); see facts ctfvtol-maxvtolheight, ctfvtol-tall-areas.

facts.title: UpStretch: jet-up links to a ledge 20 m+ at +40 cost; the Going Commando canals (17 m walls) were a one-way trap for BattleArmor
facts.fact: Going Commando (and its canal/bridge grid) has 2 m-thick walls around trenches 17 m deep (floor y=-3.5, plateau y=13.5). The planner's up-link limit is jet_gain-2 where jet_gain is learned from ground hops (9-15 m); measured full-tank burns (fuel 2.0): BA median 16.9 m, p90 18.5 m, best 34.5 m ([BOT-JETGAIN] over the 30-cell sweep). So a BA that stepped into a canal planned no way out (sw62 bot 4 stayed 127 s until it died; navfix.end_hold_frames 13601). g_upx = max(g_up+4, 20) now bounds the up-link search; a link taller than g_up costs +40 (PATH_UP_STRETCH_PEN), so ramps and plain jet-ups still win; the plan_begin 'higher goal' test no longer needs the goal within 150 m when it is 6 m+ up. facts.title: HopOut: a dry search for a jet body gets a third pass with wall hops and steep-face climbs
facts.fact: ma2_bot_path.c plan_run: when pass 1 (and PocketDrop pass 1) ends dry 10 m+ short of the goal and the body has jets (g_up>0), pass 2 (st->boost==2, <=50000 expansions) adds one-way jet-up legs (drop kind 2) from any surface: a hop over a blocked band <=12 m whose tops <= start+g_up-1, onto ground 60 m down.stretched climb up; or a climb up a face <=28 m that never rises above the landing. Cases: sw81 Ill Wind yard (raised built platform with rim colliders: no drop from built ground, goal 112 m, 48.6 s no_path), sw54 Proving Ground mesa behind a 10 m low-wall band, sw85 Rush Hour 25 m plateau over a 45-degree embankment (heavy-blocked by slope, 2 m rise per 2 m cell). A goal the pass failed to reach is memoised 20 s per start ground region. Switch RECOMP_BOT_HOP_OUT, counters hopout.* (links, climbs, found, failed, memo_skips). RECOMP_BOT_NAV_REGION now also prints an S layer (collider top per cell, capitals = hard-blocked).

facts.title: A jet-up leg that starts at the start cell had pt[0] = landing, so the controller's executor (next>0) never ran
facts.fact: plan_finish: when the first link of the route starts at the start cell itself, string pulling emitted the landing as pt[0] with drop[0]=2; Ma2Path.next starts at 0 so ctrl's `drop[next]==2 && next>0` jet-up test never fired and the body walked at the landing through the wall. LinkFoot (RECOMP_BOT_LINK_FOOT) inserts the start cell centre as pt[0] for kind-2 first legs. Plain drops (kind 1) from the start cell are not changed (walking at the landing steps off anyway).
